solves: Shows the steps of a process in order, such as a sign-up, a hiring or a setup wizard, and where the person is: the completed steps, the current one, the ones still to do and the ones with an error.
use_when: A process with steps in order and a fixed number, where the person needs to know how much is left: sign-up, hiring, setup. End it with a review step before sending.
The order is required: the linear stepper, where only the completed steps and the steps with an error are clickable.
The order is suggested: the non-linear stepper, where the pending steps are clickable too.
The label alone does not say what the step asks for, and always on an active error, to say the reason: turn on the description.
The step can be skipped: mark it optional instead of leaving it out.
At the top of a form, card or dialog, with the content of the current step right below it.
do_not_use_when: For views with no order, such as the tabs of a profile: use nph-tabs.
To show how much of a task is done with no named steps: use nph-progress.
For the place in a hierarchy: use nph-breadcrumb.
For a process of more than 7 steps: split the process.
For two steppers on the same page, or one inside the other: use one stepper at the top of the process; sub-steps stay inside the step.
For a whole sentence in the label: write one or two words, with the detail in the description.
For a vertical process: the vertical stepper waits for nph-collapsible and does not exist yet.

steps.constraint: Property only. The steps, in order, as a list of { label, description, optional, status, disabled, href }. From 2 to 7: two are allowed, the documentation asks for 3 to 7, and 7 is the maximum. label is required, already localized, one or two words. description is the support line below the label, up to two lines, and on a step with an error it says the reason. optional turns on the word Optional. status is pending, completed or error; without it the status comes from the position, completed before current and pending after it. The step at current takes no status and no disabled. disabled makes the step impossible to activate. href makes a clickable step a link; without it, a clickable step is a button. href takes http, https, mailto, tel or a relative address; any other protocol, javascript among them, in any spelling the browser reads as such, is refused. An empty list is a mount and draws nothing and says nothing. A list that is not a list, has fewer than 2 or more than 7 steps, or breaks a rule above draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

current.constraint: The position of the current step, an integer from 1 to the number of steps, the Figma property `atual`. The page sets it: the stepper keeps no state, and a click does not move it. A value outside 1 to the number of steps draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

non-linear.constraint: Off, the stepper is linear: only the completed steps and the steps with an error are clickable, to go back and review. On, the pending steps are clickable too. A disabled step and the current step are never clickable. Reflects so the consumer can style and check it.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the navigation landmark, already localized, such as Sign-up steps. It wins over the aria-label of the host. A stepper with neither draws and warns once in development.

aria-label.constraint: The accessible name of the landmark when label is not given; label wins over it. It is read by a property whose attribute is aria-label, since a property called ariaLabel is the native ARIA reflection of the element.

completed-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens a completed step, already localized, such as Completed. It is read by the screen reader and never drawn. A completed step without it draws and warns once in development.

pending-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens a pending step, already localized, such as Pending. It is also the text of a disabled step with an error, which looks pending. Without it a pending step draws and warns once in development.

error-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens a step with an error, already localized, such as With error. Without it a step with an error draws and warns once in development.

optional-label.constraint: The word Optional, already localized, drawn on a step with optional on. Without it an optional step draws without the word and warns once in development.

step-text.constraint: The text of the narrow width, already localized, with the markers {current} and {count}, such as Step {current} of {count}. The markers may come in any order the language needs. Without it the narrow width draws without the text and warns once in development.

nph-step-select.constraint: The event a button step fires when the person activates it, with detail { step }, the 1-based position of the step. It bubbles and is composed. A step with href fires only the native click, which a router handles as it handles any link. Setting current from code fires nothing. The page changes current, moves the focus to the heading of the new step and updates the page title: the stepper moves nothing by itself.

status.choose_when: completed for the steps before the current one, current for where the person is, pending for the steps after it, and error for a step that failed validation, with its reason in the description.
do_not_combine_with: a status or disabled on the current step
error with no reason in the description when the error is active

navigation.choose_when: linear (the default) when the order is required; non-linear when the order is only suggested.
do_not_combine_with: non-linear with a disabled step that the person is expected to open

rest.token: stepper/marker-background, stepper/marker-border, stepper/marker-foreground, stepper/label-foreground, stepper/marker-background-complete, stepper/marker-foreground-complete, stepper/marker-background-error, stepper/marker-foreground-error
rest.changes_for_user: Each status has its own shape: a number in a thin outline (pending), a ring and a stronger label (current), a check (completed), a triangle and the reason (error).

current.changes_for_user: A 2 px ring and a stronger label mark where the person is. It has rest only: no hover, no focus.

hover.changes_for_user: The pending and completed steps that can be activated take a background; the step with an error takes none and only underlines its label. Hover never changes the look of the status.

focus.token: stepper/focus-border, stepper/focus-border-width, stepper/focus-border-radius, stepper/focus-ring, stepper/focus-ring-width, stepper/focus-radius
focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, a border and a halo outside the step area. A focused step has no hover background.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole step is dimmed and cannot be activated. A completed step keeps its background and check; a step with an error goes back to the pending look.

business_rules: The stepper is linear by default: only the completed steps and the steps with an error are clickable. Non-linear makes the pending steps clickable too.
The page sets the current step, the status of each step and which steps are disabled. The stepper keeps no state: a click fires an event or follows a link and leaves current alone.
From 2 to 7 steps. Two are allowed; the documentation asks for 3 to 7; above 7, split the process. The stepper never collapses steps.

The text column stops at stepper/text-max-width. The label of a pending, completed or error step stays on one line and is cut with an ellipsis, and the whole text opens in nph-tooltip; the label of the current step wraps to up to two lines and is never cut. The description goes up to two lines.
The connector fills the space between the steps and never gets narrower than stepper/connector-min-width.
A clickable step is a link when it has href and a button when it has none. A button step fires nph-step-select; a link step fires only the native click.
Below 600 px of its own width the stepper becomes nph-progress of the steps type, with the text Step N of M and the label of the current step. The width counts the stepper, not the window.

Combined states: completed + disabled keeps the background and the check under the disabled opacity. Error + disabled: disabled wins, the marker goes back to the pending one and the reason shows only when the description is on. Current + disabled does not apply. Status + hover keeps the look of the status.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the piece writes no word of its own.
The vertical stepper is not part of this piece yet: it waits for nph-collapsible.
domain_errors: A steps that is not a list, or with fewer than 2 or more than 7 steps: the stepper draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.
A current that is not an integer from 1 to the number of steps: the stepper draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
A step without label, with a status outside the list, with a status or disabled on the current step, or with an unsafe href: the stepper draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

A stepper with no accessible name, a status with no hidden text, an optional step with no optional-label or no step-text for the narrow width draws and warns once in development, because the texts may arrive after the first render.

ai_hints: Use nph-stepper at the top of a form, card or dialog for a process with a fixed number of ordered steps; for views with no order use tabs, for how much is done use progress.
Give steps in order, with a short label of one or two words; put the detail in description and the reason of an error in the description of the step with an error.
Set current from the page, and change it when the person moves on; the stepper keeps no state.
Keep it linear when the order is required, and turn non-linear on only when the order is suggested.
Give each clickable step an href when the step is a page, or listen to nph-step-select when it is not; move the focus to the heading of the new step.
Give the stepper a label, or an aria-label, and the texts it owes: completed-label, pending-label, error-label, optional-label and step-text.
Do not put more than 7 steps, and do not put two steppers on the same page.

accessibility.semantics: A nav, named, holding an ordered list. Each step is a list item: a link or a button when it can be activated, and text otherwise. The current step carries aria-current step. A disabled step carries aria-disabled true. The stepper is navigation, not a tablist: it has no arrow keys. The marker is hidden from assistive technology and the position comes from the list. The connector is decorative, hidden, and has no list item of its own.
accessibility.accessible_name: The landmark: label, else the aria-label of the host. A step: the hidden status text at its start, then its label; the current step has no hidden text, since aria-current says it. The description and Optional are part of the step, so the reason of an error is read. A disabled step with an error is named as pending.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the clickable steps, in list order. The current step and the disabled steps take no Tab.
Enter activates a step. Space activates it too when it is a button; on a link, Space scrolls the page as the browser does.
The arrow keys do nothing in the stepper: each step is a Tab stop.
A pending step of the linear stepper whose label is cut takes Tab only to open the balloon with the whole label: it is not a link and Enter does nothing.
Esc closes the balloon of a cut label without moving the focus.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only, on a step that takes Tab: a border of stepper/focus-border-width in stepper/focus-border and a halo in stepper/focus-ring outside the step area, which the connector keeps from clipping. A focused step has no hover background.
accessibility.contrast: The label, the number and the description meet 4.5:1 over the background and the card, in light and dark, in every brand; the ring of the current step, the error background and the focus border meet 3:1. Inside a dialog, in dark, some brand and error colors fall below this: it is a foundation question, not a decision of the piece.
accessibility.color_alternative: Each status has its own shape and is never told by color alone: a number in a thin outline (pending), a ring and a stronger label (current), a check (completed), a triangle and the reason (error). On hover, the step with an error gets an underline.

invalid_combinations: A status or disabled on the current step — the current step is where the person is, and a blocked step cannot be it.
A steps with fewer than 2 or more than 7 steps — the stepper draws nothing.
A current outside 1 to the number of steps — the stepper draws nothing.
An href with a protocol other than http, https, mailto or tel — the stepper draws nothing.
Two steppers on the same page, or one inside the other.
A vertical stepper — it waits for nph-collapsible.

parents: the top of a form, card or dialog

anti_patterns: Using the stepper for views with no order, such as the tabs of a profile.
Putting a whole sentence in the label instead of one or two words.
Putting two steppers on the same page, or one inside the other.
Changing the number of steps in the middle of the process.
Leaving the reason of an active error out of the description.
Putting Back and Continue inside the stepper: they belong to the footer of the form.
Leaving the stepper without a label or an aria-label.
